courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Beginning Ballet
courses.description: The technique and vocabulary of classical ballet are presented. Exercises at the barre are followed by practice and combinations in the center. Previously offered as PHYA 208.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Introduction to Dance Technique
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the positions, exercises, and steps common to ballet, jazz, and modern dance. It is designed for students with no previous dance experience and is a prerequisite for EXSS 10 , 12 , and 13 . Previously offered as PHYA 212.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Beginning Modern Dance
courses.description: Students will explore the principles of movement that define modern dance, gaining some understanding of the use of weight, the shape of the body in space, an awareness of timing and energy, and individual creative potential. Previously offered as PHYA 224.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Beginning Jazz Dance
courses.description: Students will explore the roots of the jazz style through rhythm, principles of isolation and opposition, shape and energy through center work, stretches, movement across the floor, and simple routines. Previous ballet training is highly recommended. Previously offered as PHYA 220.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 11.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Beginning Social Dance
courses.description: The basic step patterns of popular social dances, such as fox trot, waltz, cha-cha, swing or shag, hustle, tango, and others are taught. Confidence in the ability to lead or to follow is developed. Social enjoyment of dance is emphasized. Previously offered as PHYA 231.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Intermediate Ballet
courses.description: For the dancer with a solid understanding of the basics of ballet and several years' dance training. It emphasizes more sophisticated steps in longer combinations. Previously offered as PHYA 308.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Intermediate Jazz Dance
courses.description: Students will explore the jazz style in greater complexity plus gain understanding of jazz music as it relates to jazz dance. It includes center work, complex movement phrases across floor, adagio, and routines using large movement vocabulary. At least two years of dance and familiarity with jazz style are recommended. Previously offered as PHYA 320.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Dance
courses.description: Students will work to develop greater technical skill and continue a more advanced exploration of modern dance principles of effort-shape through center work and phrases of greater length and complexity in the center and across the floor. At least two years of modern dance training are recommended. Previously offered as PHYA 324.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Advanced Ballet
courses.description: For the dancer with substantial background in ballet. Speed, endurance, multiple turns, beats, and complicated combinations are emphasized. Previously offered as PHYA 408.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Advanced Modern Dance
courses.description: This course is designed for the dancer with a solid understanding of the principles underlying modern dance and several years of dance training. It focuses on longer and more complicated phases of movements. Previously offered as PHYA 424.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Discrimination and Sport
courses.description: This course will examine the American ethos by looking at those who have been discriminated against in sport because of race, gender, sexual orientation, or disability.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Entrepreneurship in Human Performance and Sport
courses.description: This course will provide students an introduction to the practical entrepreneurial business tools for starting a new business (or for use in an existing organization) in the human performance and/or sport industry.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Brain Matters: The Human Computer
courses.description: The human brain remains one of the greatest anatomical and physiological mysteries remaining for us to explore. Containing over 100 billion neurons, each with 1,000-10,000 synapses, the human brain serves as the hub of everything we do. The most sophisticated 'computer' in existence, this course will provide first year students from all majors with an interdisciplinary approach to studying the human brain. Discussions will explore topics including anatomy, neurodevelopment, decision-making, maturation, disease, and more. Honors version available.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Sport Engineering and Human Performance
courses.description: This first year seminar is designed to discuss the limits of human performance and equipment that is engineered to enhance performance. How fast is it possible to run or swim? Will Olympic records continue to be broken? When do we reach our full athletic potential? This course is designed to challenge your thinking about performance using the science that governs biomechanics and human physiology as well as exploring the data that drives equipment development.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Course content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Personal Health
courses.description: Elective, open to all students. This course examines basic wellness concepts in the areas of physical fitness, nutrition, disease prevention, mental health, drug abuse, and human sexuality. Emphasis is on the individual's responsibility for his/her own health.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.description: This course is targeted to students enrolled in Department of Exercise and Sport Science majors as well as other students with interest in medical professions. This course involves a systematic approach to human anatomy and physiology with an emphasis on the musculoskeletal, articular and nervous systems as well as anatomical terminology and homeostasis. No prerequisites are required. Honors version available.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Human Anatomy
courses.description: The study of the structure of the human body with special emphasis on the musculoskeletal, articular, and nervous systems. Prosected cadaver materials are utilized to study the skeletal muscles and body viscera.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Physical Activity in Contemporary Society
courses.description: This course is designed to examine of the role of physical activity/inactivity on the health and well-being of American society. Through reading, discussion, writing and critical thinking, students will explore what it means to be physically active, the importance of physical activity, and some of the barriers and facilitators that impact the ability of various individuals to participate in physical activity.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sport and Exercise Psychology
courses.description: This course exposes students to psychological aspects contributing to sport/physical activity participation and psychological outcomes of participation. It explores psychological theories and research and their application to the affective, behavioral, and cognitive outcomes of sport/physical activity participants when considering key environmental factors.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Theory and Practice of Modern Dance Technique - Elementary-Level Elective
courses.description: An introduction to modern dance technique, history, and philosophy focusing on the physical principles of movement and their choreographic application. Students will participate in a combination of lectures and studio time.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Analysis of Sport Skills I
courses.description: A professional preparation course in the skills, knowledge, safety, and teaching progressions of basketball and soccer.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Analysis of Sport Skills II
courses.description: A professional preparation course in the skills, knowledge, safety, and teaching progressions of tennis and volleyball.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Coaching Principles
courses.description: A professional preparation course for teaching and coaching. Includes basic instruction in coaching education and principles, pedagogy for coaching, conditioning for athletes, and team building.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Health and Physical Education in the Elementary School
courses.description: This course deals with methods and materials of health and physical education in school levels kindergarten through sixth grade. Required of elementary education majors. Does not count toward physical education major.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Adapted Physical Education
courses.description: A study of problems related to body mechanics and the needs of the physically handicapped student.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Fitness Management
courses.description: Students develop a working knowledge of theories, principles, and operating procedures involved in managing programs, staff, and facilities in the health/fitness industry, including management, marketing, operations, legal aspects.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Introduction to Sport Administration
courses.description: In this course, students are introduced to the policies and problems of organizing and administering sport in public and private settings.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: International Sport Management
courses.description: Because sport cuts across all international boundaries, students must understand the global implications of the sport industry. This course introduces students to the organization, governance, business activities, and intercultural issues in international sport.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.description: This course is targeted to students enrolled in Department of Exercise and Sport Science majors as well as other students with interest in medical professions. This course involves a systematic approach to human anatomy and physiology with an emphasis on the metabolic, endocrine, digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, integumentary and immune systems.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 155.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Women and Sport
courses.description: A broad based perspective of women's participation in sport including history of participation, physiological differences, and socio-cultural influences including work, politics, family, economics, and gender roles and identity.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Fundamentals of Sports Medicine
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce the undergraduate student to the sports medicine profession and to provide the basic knowledge and skills necessary to recognize, evaluate, and treat injuries to the head and face, cervical spine, thoracic region, abdominal/urogenital region, and extremities.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175.

source.text: EXSS 265. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Research in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: An introduction to research in the fields of physical education, exercise, and sport science with emphasis on understanding and application of research findings.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Human Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: EXSS 275L is a basic human anatomy laboratory course designed to accompany EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 . For students endeavoring to major in the allied health professions.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 with a grade of B or better.

source.text: EXSS 275L. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 with a grade of B or better.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Human Physiology
courses.description: Instructor may approve equivalents for prerequisite. A lecture course in elementary physiology, covering the various systems of the body.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 175.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Emergency Care of Athletic Injuries and Illnesses
courses.description: Recommended preparation, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 . Theory and practice of basic first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and the acute care of athletic injuries.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Special Topics in EXSS
courses.description: Variable topics course in Exercise and Sports Science. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Theory and Practice of Modern Dance Technique - Intermediate-Level Elective
courses.description: An intensive study of modern dance technique and philosophy, focusing on the physical principles of movement and their choreographic application. One hour seminar and four and one-half hours laboratory.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 191; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: EXSS 291. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EXSS 191 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Internship in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide the student with a structured, supervised practical experience in exercise and sport science professional settings. Students will be individually mentored by on-site supervisors who will be responsible for assigning and assessing meaningful work, as well as providing training, feedback, and opportunities for participation in organizational activities. Students will receive guidance for professional development from their lead instructor in the form of in-class activities, assignments, and guest speakers. Restricted to EXSS general majors (not Fitness Professional or Sport Administration) with at least junior-year standing who are within 4 semesters of graduation, and a minimum 2.0 GPA (overall and within major).

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: The Art and Science of Expertise
courses.description: This course is structured around theoretical frameworks of expertise development, self-regulation, and creativity. Topics will include deliberate practice, the psychology of motivation and positive functioning, accountability, personal narratives, competitiveness, leadership, resilience, flow, learned optimism, performance measurement, well-being, and the role of creativity and design in solving complex problems. Students will learn to compose, design, build, present, or perform a work that reflects immersion in their chosen domain of expertise; to explain the influence of creativity, technologies, materials, and processes on performance and expression; and to evaluate their own and others' work through structured critique to create value in creative domains.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Fundamentals of Sport Marketing
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to marketing within the sports industry, including the unique aspects of the sport product and sport consumer markets.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 221.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sport Facility and Event Management
courses.description: This course is designed to develop practical competencies necessary for effectively managing sport facilities and events while providing students with experiential learning opportunities inside and outside the classroom.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 221.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Finance and Economics of Sport
courses.description: This course provides an understanding of the financial and economic growth of sport, economic theory applied to the sport industry, and the basic principles and methods of sound fiscal control.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, ECON 101 and EXSS 221; Pre- or corequisite, STOR 151 or STOR 155 recommended.

source.text: EXSS 324. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, ECON 101 and EXSS 221 ; Pre- or corequisite, STOR 151 or STOR 155 recommended.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: The Role of Intercollegiate Athletics in Higher Education
courses.description: This course is designed to help students interested in working in college sports understand what that role has been and might be in the future, with an emphasis on maximizing the educational value of intercollegiate athletic participation and the integration of athletics with academic and student life dimensions on college campuses.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Legal Aspects of Sport
courses.description: This course provides a foundation in general legal concepts and familiarizes students with the legal areas they are most likely to encounter as managers in the sports and fitness industry.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 221.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Predictive Analytics in Sport
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with an introduction to predictive analytics utilizing regression-based modeling approaches. As a CURE course, students will learn the iterative process of model building through trial and error and by working with other students on hands-on problems. At the conclusion of this course, students will be able to analyze sport-related data using predictive analytics, whether the dependent variable is continuous or binary in nature. Honors version available.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, STOR 151 or 155 with a grade of B or better.

source.text: EXSS 327. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, STOR 151 or 155 with a grade of B or better. | RESEARCH.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sport Business Venture
courses.description: This course will provide students an introduction to practical entrepreneurial business tools for starting a new business (or for use in an existing organization) in the sport industry.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sport Communication
courses.description: This course introduces students to professional communication in sport contexts. Contexts of focus are media (i.e., broadcast and digital) and organizations related to sport. Through readings, in-class activities, lectures, group projects, and guest speakers, students learn about the development of communication professions and practices in sport media and organizations, strategic approaches to communication challenges and opportunities in these contexts, the role of research and social forces in sport communication, and vocational paths in sport communication.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sociocultural Aspects of Sport and Exercise
courses.description: This course will enhance students' understandings about social and cultural dimensions of sport and exercise contexts. Through directed readings, classroom conversations, assignments/projects, and guest speakers, students in this course will learn how these sociocultural realities 1) are explored through academic research, and 2) impact sport and exercise policy, programs, and innovation, and 3) impact sport and exercise constituents, such as participants, planners, leaders, and advocates. This is an elective course for all junior/senior EXSS majors.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sports Nutrition
courses.description: The role of nutrition in maximizing physical performance, promoting health, and controlling body weight. Includes individual nutritional assessments.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 256 or EXSS 276 or NUTR 240.

source.text: EXSS 360. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EXSS 256 or EXSS 276 or NUTR 240 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Foundations of Sports Medicine Rehabilation
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce undergraduate students to the basic principles and skills used to rehabilitate sport related injuries with an emphasis on musculoskeletal injuries.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 265.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Therapeutic Modalities
courses.description: This is an advanced athletic training course, designed to provide the athletic training student with knowledge and skills necessary for treating injuries.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 265, EXSS 288, and EXSS 366.

source.text: EXSS 367. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 ; and EXSS 265 , EXSS 288 , and EXSS 366 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Therapeutic Exercise and Rehabilitation
courses.description: This is an advanced athletic training course, designed to provide the athletic training student with knowledge and skills necessary for rehabilitating injuries.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 265, EXSS 288, EXSS 366, and EXSS 367.

source.text: EXSS 368. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 ; and EXSS 265 , EXSS 288 , EXSS 366 , and EXSS 367 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Athletic Training Seminar
courses.description: A presentation of the historical and current perspectives on athletic training, including techniques for organizing and administering athletic training programs.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 288.

source.text: EXSS 369. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 ; and EXSS 288 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: General Medicine in Athletic Training
courses.description: Advanced course focusing on understanding instrumentation used in assessing internal injury related to sport. Pharmacology, drug testing, psychosocial interventions, and selected emergency procedures pertaining to athletic injury are also presented.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 265 and EXSS 288.

source.text: EXSS 370. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 , or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 ; and EXSS 265 and EXSS 288 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Physiological Basis of Human Performance
courses.description: Instructor may approve equivalents for EXSS prerequisites. Students must take laboratory section along with class. The application of physiological principles to sport and physical activity. Both immediate and chronic adaptations to exercise are studied. Two lecture and two laboratory hours a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

source.text: EXSS 376. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 ; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Neuromuscular Control and Learning
courses.description: This course introduces neuromuscular control and motor learning through a general understanding of neuroanatomy/neurophysiology, sensory contributions to human movement, initiation and regulation of voluntary movement, and the acquisition of motor skills. Course topics include central and peripheral nervous system functions in the production and regulation of human movement, neural pathways and control mechanisms, and enhancement of motor learning in the rehabilitation and training settings. Honors version available.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175.

source.text: EXSS 380. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Biomechanics of Sport
courses.description: This course introduces the principles of biomechanics, including kinematics, kinetics, projectile motion, fluid forces and statics analysis. It includes the application of both kinematics and kinetic variables to joint motion and sport activities. Instructor may approve equivalents for EXSS prerequisite.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175.

source.text: EXSS 385. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Undergraduate Learning Assistanship
courses.description: This course is designed for undergraduate students to provide course support to their peers. This course provides opportunities for students to prepare, demonstrate, and consult with their peers via in- and out-of-class activities. Students will gain an enhanced understanding of Exercise and Sport Science content with a lens towards explaining to less experienced students, gaining pedagogical knowledge and experience, and engaging in comprehensive, concise, and clear oral and written communication. EXSS Majors only; Successful completion, with a grade of C or higher, of the course you are assisting.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sports Medicine Clinical
courses.description: This field experience offers implementation of theories and practices of athletic training and sports medicine under the supervision of a certified athletic trainer.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 265 or EXSS 288.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 5 total credits. 5 total completions.

source.text: EXSS 393. | 1-3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 ; and EXSS 265 or EXSS 288 . | HI-INTERN.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Course
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Majors preferred. Laboratory/research study addressing exercise and sport science questions. Requires final written report. Repeatable for six total credits.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Independent Studies in Exercise and Sport Science Elective
courses.description: Required preparation, any two relevant courses. Permission of the instructor. Individually designed in-depth study in an area of interest within exercise and sport science. Available to both majors and nonmajors under the supervision of selected EXSS faculty members.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Critical Analysis of Literature in Sport and Exercise Psychology
courses.description: This course will expose students to research in sport and exercise psychology using the C.R.E.A.T.E. (Consider, Read, Elucidate the hypotheses, Analyze and interpret the data, and Think of the next Experiment) framework. Students will follow the historical publications of one sport and exercise psychology research group to better understand the research process. Each research paper will be digested/critiqued in phases. Student will also formulate their own novel research questions and present them to the class.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 181.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Theory and Application of Strength Training and Conditioning for Fitness Professionals
courses.description: Students will learn to design an individualized fitness plan for a "healthy" adult for common fitness goals by assessing their movement and fitness, exercise leadership, and program design. This class, in part, prepares students for the NASM certified personal training (CPT) certification.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

source.text: EXSS 408. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 ; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Exercise Prescription for Special Populations
courses.description: Exercise benefits everybody. This course will teach evidence-based information for developing, modifying and implementing fitness programs for individuals with chronic disease, metabolic, cardiac, pulmonary, and other issues deemed as special populations. The knowledge and skills attained in this course will enhance any basic personal training certification and give a better understanding of working with what could be considered the general public.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 376.

source.text: EXSS 409. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 , or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 ; and EXSS 376 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription
courses.description: This course is designed to provide theoretical and practical knowledge in basic exercise testing and prescription for both healthy and select special populations. This course includes both lectures and a lab. Priority registration is given to EXSS- Fitness Professional students and permission to enroll is obtained by completing the form linked in the registration section in Connect Carolina.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 376.

source.text: EXSS 410. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 , or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 ; and EXSS 376 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Athlete Performance and Sport Science
courses.description: This course invites students who are passionate about sport to explore how data science is transforming athletic performance. You will examine how data-driven approaches optimize strength, conditioning, physiology, psychology, nutrition, and overall wellness. Through hands-on projects and applied case studies, you will learn to track physical performance, monitor health and recovery, and analyze psychological factors that influence success.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisite, EXSS 273, PSYC 210, or appropriate statistics course with permission of instructor.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Program Planning in Recreation Services
courses.description: This experiential course covers the concepts and skills used in program planning. Students apply their program planning skills to real-life situations and implement a recreation program for a community agency. Previously offered as RECR 420.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sport Sales and Revenue Production Seminar
courses.description: This course will analyze and produce skills essential to the revenue production and sales process commonly found in the sport business. In this class students will develop an understanding and appreciation for the sales and revenue-production process related to a sport franchise and/or organization.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 221 and EXSS 322.

source.text: EXSS 424. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 221 and EXSS 322 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Introduction to Leadership and Group Dynamics
courses.description: An analysis of the techniques, methods, and motives of group and community leaders. Special attention is focused upon the roles of organizational structure, personnel policies, and in-service training programs. Previously offered as RECR 430.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EXSS 221.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Exercise Technique
courses.description: This course is designed to teach students how to lead and coach a group of individuals toward movement proficiency in common athletic-based exercises.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

source.text: EXSS 433L. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 ; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Essentials of Corrective Exercise Training
courses.description: Students will learn to explain, design, and execute a corrective exercise program to improve movement quality. Students will be introduced to skills such as range of motion, strength, and movement quality assessments. This class, in-part, prepares students for the NASM corrective exercise specialist (CES) certification.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

source.text: EXSS 450. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 ; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Functional Anatomy
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of joint mechanics. It exposes students to motions of the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine as well as the extremities, and relates these concepts to movement of the body during specific activities.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 385.

source.text: EXSS 475. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 , or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 ; and EXSS 385 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Sports Performance Training
courses.description: This course focuses on the foundational knowledge needed to train athletes, including performance assessment, coaching exercise technique, and program design. This class, in part, prepares students for the NSCA Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) certification.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

source.text: EXSS 478. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 ; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276 .

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Performance Enhancement Specialization for Health Professionals
courses.description: This course is designed for certified athletic trainers (ATC) and gives them advanced rehab and performance skills that can be used during an athlete's return to sport progression. Students will learn to assess movement quality and performance, lead an individual through common strength and conditioning exercises, and write a basic performance plan based on NASM strategies. This class, in-part, prepares students for the NASM performance enhancement specialist (PES) certification.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Data Science Applications in Exercise, Sport, and Movement Science
courses.description: The goal of this course is to give students an introduction to and hands-on experience with all phases of the data science process and applications to exercise, sport, and movement science. Topics that will be covered include data formats, loading, and cleaning. This course will also concentrate on the concepts and structures necessary to design and implement a database system as well as basic programming with open source software to help navigate databases and conduct basic analyses. Fundamental ethical issues in data science will also be covered.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Exercise Endocrinology
courses.description: Advanced course examining the responses of the endocrine system to exercise and the adaptations that occur with exercise training. Provides the fundamentals necessary for exercise science and allied health science students to understand the integral role that the endocrine system plays in exercise.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Neuromechanics of Human Movement
courses.description: This course explores interactions between the nervous and musculoskeletal systems via integration of concepts from neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, anatomy, neuromuscular control, and biomechanics. Topics include muscle mechanics, sensorimotor function, joint stability, movement disorders, neurocognition, and neuroplasticity following injury and disease.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Biopsychosocial Aspects of Sport Injury
courses.description: This course is designed to explore the theory and research related to the biopsychosocial approach to treating patients experiencing sport injury and undergoing rehabilitation. Application and synthesis of biopsychosocial theories and biopsychosocial therapy interventions into sport injury research and clinical practice will occur. The focus is on theory and application of various psychological concepts.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Neurotrauma Involving the Head and Neck: Overview of Neurophysiology, Assessment, and Management
courses.description: This course is designed to expand on graduate and upper-level undergraduate student's foundational knowledge to provide an advanced overview of neurotrauma associated anatomy, physiology, assessment, and management associated with sports and physical activity, with a specific focus on concussion and cervical spine/spinal cord injury. The course will include higher level concepts, application, and synthesis of knowledge concerning these areas of focus.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Applied Statistics and Research Methods in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: Required preparation, undergraduate statistics course. Applied statistical analysis - interpretation of data from exercise and sport science. Emphasis: choosing method of analysis, using statistics software to run analyses. Major topics: experimental and nonexperimental research design, sampling, hypothesis testing, power calculation, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation, simple and multiple regression, and chi square.

courses.subject: EXSS
courses.title: Research Design and Methods
courses.description: Required preparation, any undergraduate statistics course. Builds heavily upon material presented in EXSS 700 . Planning, conducting, and reporting of research. Thesis writing and writing for publication. Problem-solving and practical experience in applied statistical analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data from the field of exercise and sport science.
